metadata.description: Full workspace build: every project's `build`, ordered by the task graph, followed by the whole-tree ESM packaging assertions. Referenced by .circleci/config.yml and by the dbx-claude build recovery target (.dbx-claude/dbx-claude.json).  This used to be a hand-sequenced chain -- `build-api-dependency-chain` (util -> rxjs/model/date -> firebase -> nestjs -> firebase-server -> oauth-resource), then `build-dependency-chain` (+ dbx-core, dbx-web), then an `--exclude=demo-api` sweep, then demo-api last -- and those targets' own descriptions said outright that they existed because the graph edges did not. They do now: every package family and every app carries real `dependsOn` edges (parent `build-base` -> `^build`, child `build-base` -> its parent, parent `build` -> its children), so one scheduler derives the order, dedupes shared tasks and parallelizes what is genuinely independent. Re-introducing a hand-written chain here would only serialize work the graph already knows how to order.  verify-esm-exports runs SECOND and as its own command (not a dependsOn entry -- dependsOn does not order its own entries): its assertions are only valid once EVERYTHING is built, because a parent package's `exports` names subpaths that other projects compile into its dist.
Runs the fast oxlint tier over every project (the `oxlint` target inferred by @nx/oxlint). Complements lint-all rather than replacing it — see the adopt-the-nx-oxlint-plugin plan for the tier split.

Lint every project with oxlint via dbx-cli-lint-cache, writing grouped JSON caches to .tmp/lint-cache/*.oxlint.json (plus index.oxlint.json). This is what makes the oxlint tier visible to dbx-claude-lint-read; without it an oxlint target is a linter nothing runs.
Lint every project via dbx-cli-lint-cache with --fix, writing grouped JSON caches to .tmp/lint-cache/. Rebuilds the CLI bundle first if its source changed.

metadata.description: Whole-tree ESM packaging assertions over the built dist: every `exports` target exists on disk, no CommonJS artifacts survived, and every directory holding ambiguous `.js` sits in a package scope declaring the module type. This is the `--mode=verify` half of tools/scripts/finalize-esm-exports.mjs. It lives at the workspace level because the assertions are only valid once EVERYTHING is built -- a parent package `exports` names its subpaths, so asserting the moment the parent finishes would report subpath targets that have not been built yet. `build-all` runs it as its final step, which is what makes these assertions actually fire in CI.  The `--mode=rewrite` half stays unused on purpose: it rewrites only the directory it is handed, and subpath entry points have no `build` of their own to finalize their nested package.json, so the 19 per-package callers keep the no-flag (rewrite + verify) form. Companion to check-esm-imports.
